title: How World Wide Stereo builds trust into every purchase
summary: In an era of consumer skepticism, World Wide Stereo built customer trust by pairing decades of hands-on service with a seamless product protection integration
body_markdown:
If you sell premium home technology online, trust matters as much as the products you sell. Earn it, and customers stay with you for years. Everything else you do is built on it.


World Wide Stereo has understood that from the start.


The company has spent more than 45 years working at it, and they sum up their customer service philosophy in one phrase: do well by doing good. That idea shaped a culture built on great customer service, and on the belief that treating people well is good business. You can see it in how the company functions, at a time when[trust matters more than ever](https://www.surebright.com/blog/trust-recession-in-ecommerce-why-building-trust-with-customers-is-harder-than-ever) .


So, we sat down with Chief Marketing Officer Emily Cole to learn how the brand keeps building that trust, and why product protection was a natural next step.


Here are some highlights from our conversation.


## Inside World Wide Stereo's approach to customer trust


In their own words, the company has been “[Enhancing the way people experience home](https://www.worldwidestereo.com/pages/about-us?srsltid=AfmBOoooTCVPKkq67vdXUamXl5ksW2dLqWM2EqGioFeW6KLeVE85f9yq) ” for almost half a century, from helping customers discover exceptional audio and video to designing and integrating complete home technology experiences that bring together entertainment, lighting, shading, control, security, and more.


The brand carries some of the most respected names in the business:[Bowers & Wilkins,](https://www.worldwidestereo.com/collections/bowers-and-wilkins/)[Sonus faber](https://www.worldwidestereo.com/collections/sonus-faber) ,[McIntosh](https://www.worldwidestereo.com/collections/McIntosh) ,[Sony](https://www.worldwidestereo.com/collections/Sony) ,[Focal](https://www.worldwidestereo.com/collections/focal-audio) , the names you find in the homes of serious audiophiles.


These are premium purchases, and customers treat them that way.


If you think of yourself in the shoes of a customer choosing a $5,000 amplifier or a new speaker setup, you'll also want to know will the product perform, and that the store will still be there for them long after the sale.


*" From the beginning, our mission has been simple,"* answers Emily, *"help people make confident technology decisions and deliver an experience that’s as exceptional as the products we sell. Whether someone visits one of our showrooms or shops with us online, we want them to feel the same level of expertise, personal guidance, and support before, during, and long after the purchase."*


Trust starts with the basics, and World Wide Stereo has offered them for years: 60-day returns and exchanges that give buyers time to be sure about a purchase, a price-match guarantee that keeps pricing fair and competitive, free shipping on every order, and trained, certified salespeople and technicians who help buyers decide.


The team also goes further than that, building trust in a way that keeps customers coming back.


*“It starts with understanding what the customer is trying to achieve, whether that’s choosing the right pair of speakers or designing a fully integrated technology experience throughout the home,”* shares Emily.


From there, they offer education, product recommendations, installation support when needed, and ongoing service after the purchase.


*“Our goal is for customers to feel supported long after the product arrives or the project is completed.”*


That is where SureBright came in. Product protection plans were built right into the buying process as a clear, simple choice. The goal is peace of mind, so customers can enjoy a big purchase knowing help is still there if they need it.


All it took was choosing the right partner.


*“Our priority was finding a solution that added confidence without adding complexity: simple for customers to understand, easy for our team to manage, and seamless within our ecommerce experience.”*


That is exactly what SureBright delivered. Talking about how both companies suited each other's ethos, the Emily shared:


*“SureBright fits naturally into our online checkout experience and complements the consultative approach we take with customers. Because the offering is presented clearly and at the appropriate point in the buying journey, customers can make an informed decision without adding friction to the purchasing process."*


In ecommerce, an easy checkout is worth real money. Across the industry it adds up: an estimated[$18 billion annually to cart abandonment alone](https://www.bigcommerce.com/articles/ecommerce/abandoned-carts/) . World Wide Stereo has always understood this, so they chose a protection plan that fits naturally into the way people already shop with them.


*"What stood out most was their willingness to work closely with our team to ensure the integration aligned with our customer experience goals rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach."*


### The result


World Wide Stereo saw a change in how buyers acted right away:


*"Customer confidence and loyalty have likely seen the biggest impact. When customers know they have additional protection available, they often feel more comfortable making a purchase and are more likely to return to us for future purchases."*


That matters even more with the premium products World Wide Stereo sells.


## What other brands can learn from World Wide Stereo


If you sell premium or high-tech products online, you are already in the trust business.


Your product photos, your return policy, how fast you reply, and the emails you send after a sale all shape how confident a shopper feels about buying.


Protection plans are one of the most useful tools you have, and World Wide Stereo has shown how well they work for a specialty store.


Emily shared that the right partner can enhance the customer experience rather than complicate it. According to her:


*"A protection plan should be easy to understand, easy to purchase, and supported by a team that is responsive when questions arise. If the program creates confidence for customers and simplicity for your team, it's much more likely to succeed."*


Asked why they chose SureBright, Emily said the answer came down to three things:


*"Trust, transparency, and execution. Customers are relying on both the retailer and the protection provider when they make a purchase. The right partner offers clear coverage, a straightforward claims process, strong customer support, and a seamless experience from start to finish."*


That is exactly what a customer remembers when they decide to buy again or refer a friend.


## Doing well by doing good


The same thinking that shaped how World Wide Stereo built its business also shaped how it picks its partners.


They earned trust by pairing the selection of a big national store with the know-how and personal service of a local specialty shop. Protection plans carry that promise a little further, so customers know the help continues once the purchase is home.


Doing good and doing well were always the same thing. Both are ways of honoring the trust customers place in them.
